security_lab.target: labs/corpus_storage/src/storage.c (ss_skip_put, ss_skip_get, ss_skip_erase, ss_skip_scan, ss_height, ss_random, ss_random_advance declared in labs/corpus_storage/storage.h)

security_lab.violated_property: Ordered-map integrity and bounded work: level zero holds every key exactly once in increasing order, erase removes the key from every level so it is no longer visible, replacement preserves height, and a deterministic generator must not be presented as a secret; worst-case traversal stays bounded by 32 nodes even when all heights are one.

security_lab.target: labs/corpus_ecc (src/ecc.c: ec_encode, ec_decode, ec_erasures, interleave and deinterleave), a local original teaching provider.
security_lab.adversary: Knows the public encoding and can flip or replace every bit of a transmitted codeword or four-lane frame (including three or four flips, wrong-phase and burst placement), and can encode a payload of their choice such as 9; holds no secret key and cannot change the decoder, pointers or the application policy.
security_lab.violated_property: Authorization and integrity of message authority: the decoder only provides error correction, so a forged or replaced valid codeword is accepted as an authentic payload, a three-bit pattern is miscorrected to a different payload instead of being detected, and a four-bit pattern can turn one valid word into another.
security_lab.boundary: Local arrays and synthetic payloads in one hosted process with no device, radio, file or network. The registered anchors (ecc_tests, tests.c) print only an ECC_FULL, ECC_ERASURES or ECC_BURST_LIMITS marker; harmless success is a decode status and payload value that your own harness prints.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Backed by the learner-visible anchor corpus_ecc.burst (labs/corpus_ecc/tests.c, ECC_BURST_LIMITS; marker ECC_CHECK): ec_encode(8, 9, &forged) == EC_OK followed by ec_decode(8, forged, &r) == EC_OK with r.data == 9; ec_decode(8, 7, &r) == EC_CORRECTED with r.data != 0 (zero word XOR 7 miscorrected); ec_decode(8, 135, &r) == EC_OK with r.data != 0 (a valid word); a frame interleaved at phase 1 and deinterleaved at phase 0 decoding lane 0 as EC_OK with data != 0, and deinterleave phase 4 returning EC_INVALID. The corpus_ecc.8 and corpus_ecc.16 anchors check that two distinct flips return EC_DETECTED with the output sentinel 99 unchanged. The burst anchor asserts exactly one three-flip instance (word 7, the zero word with three bits flipped, tests.c:176) and one four-flip instance (word 135, a weight-4 word that is itself the valid encoding of payload 1, tests.c:177); general three- and four-flip behaviour is not asserted, so derive it from the distance-4 argument and your own harness. The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation: the supplied corpus_ecc.burst anchor demonstrates, for the specified words 7, 135 and the forged payload 9, that the claimed message-authority property fails; no memory fault, secret disclosure or privilege change occurs, so it is not a crash, sanitizer-finding or proved-impact.
security_lab.remediation: State error correction as separate from authority, limiting the guarantee to at most two flips and known erasures within 2t+s<4. The anchors corpus_ecc.8, corpus_ecc.16, corpus_ecc.erasures and corpus_ecc.burst retain both forged encodings and the miscorrection cases; any application range check (rejecting 9 under a zero-only policy) must be your own added test, and does not stop a forgery in the authorized range.
security_lab.limitations: Does not model a radio channel or physical coding, does not show that a range check stops an authorized-range forgery, and provides no authentication, identity or replay protection; interleaving only bounds bursts of length at most 4.

security_lab.target: labs/corpus_money (src/money.c: validation, checked addition, rational rescaling, largest-remainder allocation and staged settlement per money.h), a local original synthetic-account teaching provider.
security_lab.adversary: Chooses the currency code, scale and amount of each Money value, allocation weights (including zero and overflowing sums), destination account indices (including duplicates and invalid ones), the rounding mode, and the failure cut passed to the staged settlement. Cannot modify account storage directly, choose pointers or reach any real account or credential.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of value conservation and publication: addition and allocation must never mix currencies or scales, the sum of all involved balances must be conserved on success, no intermediate stage may become visible, and an aborted or overflowing settlement (including a late credit overflow) must leave every account unchanged.
security_lab.boundary: Local hosted process using synthetic accounts and small integer amounts plus the signed extrema, built from a disposable CMake directory; no real accounts, credentials, network target or host security change, and harmless success is a printed balance or snapshot mismatch.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Backed by the learner-visible anchors corpus_money.currency and corpus_money.settlement (labs/corpus_money/tests.c; marker CM_CHECK): cm_make with code "usd" or scale 10 returns CM_INVALID; cm_add on values with currency or scale mismatching (currency[0] altered to 'E', or scale 3) returns CM_INVALID; cm_add(INT64_MAX, 1) and cm_add(INT64_MIN, -1) return CM_OVERFLOW leaving b.minor == 77; cm_settle with cut 0..3 returns CM_ABORTED with the accounts memcmp-unchanged; a duplicate destination index returns CM_INVALID unchanged; amount 9 returns CM_FUNDS unchanged; and with a[3] = INT64_MAX a late credit overflow returns CM_OVERFLOW with all accounts unchanged. For the failing case, build a defective variant (mixed-unit add reported as success, or settlement that writes accounts before all credits are checked) and show these CHECKs reject it (labs/corpus_money/reject.py requires exit 1, CM_CHECK and no sanitizer output). Compare balances to your own rational model.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a defective variant the learner builds (the supplied anchors corpus_money.currency and corpus_money.settlement pass on a correct provider and no flawed provider is supplied): conservation or unchanged-on-refusal then fails on a named input in the synthetic ledger, but there is no memory fault so it is not a crash or sanitizer-finding, and it does not show a real-account effect, authentication bypass or arbitrary code execution so it is not proved-impact.
security_lab.remediation: Check currency and scale before checked addition, preflight allocation and every credit before writing any account, and return CM_ABORTED or CM_OVERFLOW with accounts unchanged. The existing anchors corpus_money.currency and corpus_money.settlement (mismatch add, cuts 0..3, duplicate destination and late overflow CHECKs) must reject the learner-built defective variants.
security_lab.limitations: A semantic credit violation is not code execution, external-service authentication bypass or crash durability; constant-time behaviour is not claimed, the synthetic ledger is not a payment system, and the finite cases do not prove arbitrary correctness.

security_lab.target: labs/foundation_depth/src/depth.c (fd_apply), with the supplied flawed teaching control labs/foundation_depth/drills/authorization.c (function `vulnerable`, run by the always-built executable depth-authorization, which the learner runs directly).
security_lab.adversary: Controls the 8-byte wire record bytes (count, value, flags), the declared length, the ordering and repetition of requests, and whether authorization is denied. Does not control the trusted authorization value, the executable, the counter pointer or host memory.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of protected state: the synthetic counter must change only on a fully admitted, authorized request whose proposed result old + count * value fits in int32_t, and every failure preserves the old counter.
security_lab.boundary: Ordinary local process, no sockets, secrets or elevated privilege. The flawed `vulnerable` path and the repaired fd_apply path live in one executable (depth-authorization, drills/authorization.c:17-58) and each acts on its own synthetic int32_t counter starting at 10 (authorization.c:44-45); the registered defense test (tests/tests.c:645-688) resets its counter to 10 before the length, opcode and flag-bit trials.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (b) The supplied control labs/foundation_depth/drills/authorization.c (CMake target depth-authorization, built unconditionally at labs/foundation_depth/CMakeLists.txt:36-37; run the executable directly, because its CTest registration foundation_depth.authorization_observation exists only in assessor builds (CMakeLists.txt:51-53) and is not learner evidence) defines `vulnerable` (lines 17-38), which commits the counter before checking authorization; on attacker bytes 01 00 00 02 00 00 00 03 with old counter 10 and authorization 0 it returns FD_DENIED with counter 16, while fd_apply returns FD_DENIED with counter 10; the executable exits 0 only when both statuses are FD_DENIED and the flawed path ends at 16 and the repaired path at 10 (authorization.c:55-57). (a) The learner-visible test `defense` in labs/foundation_depth/tests/tests.c (CTest foundation_depth.defense) requires FD_DENIED with counter 10, then FD_OK with counter 16 on authorization, FD_RANGE with counter 10 for every length 0..9 except 8 and for the overflow record, FD_INVALID with counter 10 for the bad opcode byte and flag bit, and FD_DENIED then FD_OK leaving 10 for the zero-delta record.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation: the supplied control authorization.c demonstrates a rejected request changing the counter (flawed path ends at 16 after FD_DENIED), which violates the stated integrity property, but it is a defined logic error with no memory fault and no effect beyond one synthetic integer, so it is not a sanitizer finding, undefined behaviour or proved impact.
security_lab.remediation: Run every admission gate and the checked arithmetic first and perform one commit after authorization. The supplied defense test never calls the drill's `vulnerable`; it exercises fd_apply only. If you write a commit-first fd_apply, the first denial in foundation_depth.defense (`fd_apply(valid, sizeof valid, 0, &counter)` followed by CHECK(counter == 10), tests/tests.c:649-650) is where it should fail, and the same witness bytes are replayed against the repaired fd_apply by authorization.c:48-49.
security_lab.limitations: Shows nothing about caller pointer validity, concurrent callers, the integrity of the authorization input or any production protocol; sanitizers would not detect this defined logic error, and the flawed variant is a supplied teaching control, not production code.

security_lab.target: labs/network_followthrough/src/ip.c (ni_init, ni_receive, ni_take, ni_tick) over the contract in labs/network_followthrough/ip/CONTRACTS.md.
security_lab.adversary: Controls the fragments of locally constructed packet arrays: identification, protocol, offsets and lengths, arrival order, overlap content and arrival times. Does not control the two 1480-byte slots, the 60000 ms absolute lifetime, the checksum provider or any host or network state.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of reassembly and bounded ownership: fragments with different identity (for example ICMP and TCP with the same ID) must never mix, no datagram is delivered while a hole remains, overlap is poisoned or only accepted when bytes match, and the lifetime never refreshes.
security_lab.boundary: Local arrays, the host author harness or the emulated strict Cortex-M4 packet model, synthetic payload bytes only; no packet is sent, no real interface is opened and no board is required for this exercise.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) Public test labs/network_followthrough/ip/tests.c, function reassembly (CTest network_followthrough.ip): fragments at offsets 0 and 16 of a 24-byte payload both return NI_WAIT and only the offset-8 fragment returns NI_OK, after which ni_take gives length 44 with payload bytes 0..23 and a valid header checksum; a TCP fragment (protocol 6) with the same ID as an ICMP one (protocol 1) lands in a different slot (index 1); a conflicting overlap returns NI_CONFLICT and leaves slot 0 NI_POISON; in NI_IDENTICAL mode a flipped byte returns NI_CONFLICT; a second fragment at 59999 keeps expiry 60000, ni_tick(60000) frees the slot and ni_tick backwards returns NI_INVALID. (c) Flawed variants (ID-only keying, hole-tolerant delivery, lifetime refresh) are learner-built, as the contract's D3 requires rejected compiled mutants; each should fail the check above that matches it.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only by the learner-built flawed variants (none is supplied; the public test network_followthrough.ip only passes on a correct reassembler): a variant that keys on ID alone or tolerates holes would deliver mixed or premature data, which breaks the stated reassembly property in the teaching target, but this is a logic error with no memory fault and no external effect, so it is not a sanitizer finding or proved impact.
security_lab.remediation: Key slots on the full source, destination, protocol and ID tuple, deliver only on complete coverage and expire from the first fragment; the existing test network_followthrough.ip (the reassembly CHECKs for NI_WAIT before the last fragment, the separate-slot index == 1, NI_POISON and expiry == 60000 in labs/network_followthrough/ip/tests.c) must reject each learner-built mutant.
security_lab.limitations: No supplied flawed variant exists, so violations are shown only on mutants the learner builds; it does not show a fragment attack on any real stack, forwarding behaviour or real-clock timing, and the Time Exceeded report is claimed only under its documented premises.

security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of the controller's congestion invariants: committed flight is tracked independently of cwnd and rwnd, cwnd grows only on valid new acknowledgements, duplicates do not inflate it beyond the specified rules, and an unauthenticated ACK stream cannot make the sender exceed what the contract allows.

security_lab.target: labs/b04_depth/src/depth.c (b4_framing) with the public test labs/b04_depth/tests/tests.c.
security_lab.adversary: Controls up to 512 synthetic header-section bytes: Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding fields, header case, whitespace before the colon, duplicates, unsupported codings, overflowing lengths, bare LF and truncation. Does not control the parser harness, the two decision models, the caller's close decision or any listener.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of message boundary agreement: one byte sequence must have one next-message boundary, so a parser that accepts both Content-Length and chunked framing makes two models consume different byte counts for the same message.
security_lab.boundary: Local process on fixed synthetic bytes (framing, labs/b04_depth/tests/tests.c:83-145); no listener, socket, file, fork or external request. The only disagreement shown is between two boundary values written in the test, not between two running parsers.
security_lab.expected_evidence:
(a) Public test labs/b04_depth/tests/tests.c, function framing (CTest b04_depth.framing): it sets the CL-first boundary to the literal 6 and sets the zero-chunk boundary to 5 after comparing the first five bytes of the body `0

SYNTHETIC` with `0

` by hand (tests.c:87-95), then requires 6 != 5 and that byte 6 is 'S'; neither value is produced by b4_framing or by a parser, so the two recipients are arithmetic stand-ins; b4_framing on `Content-Length: 6` plus `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` must return B4_CONFLICT with the output struct still {9, 99}; the table requires B4_CONFLICT for duplicate lengths and `chunked, gzip`, B4_RANGE for a too-large and an overflowing length, B4_INVALID for `Content-Length : 1`, `+1`, bare LF and trailing bytes, always with the output unchanged, and every truncation of `Content-Length: 3` must fail with body still 99. (c) Variant to build yourself, stated as the property to break: a b4_framing that returns B4_OK, or fills the output struct, for the Content-Length plus Transfer-Encoding pair; the CONFLICT CHECK (tests.c:99-101) is where you should predict the failure and then confirm it by running b04_depth.framing. No supplied artifact contains such a parser.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation: the supplied test shows only that two hand-written boundary values differ for the same bytes, and a parser that accepts both framing headers exists only once the learner builds it; in either case exploitation needs differently interpreting forwarding recipients that this lab does not build, so request smuggling and proved impact are not shown.
security_lab.remediation: Reject any message carrying both framing headers with B4_CONFLICT, publish nothing and leave the close decision explicit to the caller; the existing test b04_depth.framing (the CONFLICT CHECK on `Content-Length: 6` plus `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and the table of duplicate, case, whitespace, overflow and truncation inputs in labs/b04_depth/tests/tests.c) must reject the accepting variant.
security_lab.limitations: Shows disagreement between two inline bounded models only; the boundary arithmetic is in the test, not a forwarding proxy, so it does not show smuggling against real servers, TLS behaviour, or arbitrary code execution, and it covers the narrow complete-field grammar only.

exercises.title: Control-flow joins and the limits of bytecode verification

environment.language: C17; explicitly labeled C23 comparison only
environment.target: Linux x86-64 hosted bounded model
environment.dependencies: Original mechanism uses type/limit headers; libc/Python/ctypes are host verification dependencies.

security_lab.target: labs/b05_depth/src/depth.c (b5_verify) over 16-instruction synthetic bytecode records.
security_lab.adversary: Controls every record of a program of at most 16 instructions: opcode, operand and jump or branch target, including two paths that reach one PC at different stack heights and unreachable invalid opcodes. Does not control the verifier, the stack limit of 8, the entry height 0 or any execution engine.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of the verification guarantee: an accepted program must have a single consistent stack height at every join and structurally valid records, so a verifier that checks each path separately accepts a program whose later behaviour depends on the path taken.
security_lab.boundary: Hosted bounded model with fixed synthetic records; programs are only verified, never executed, with no JIT, native code or system call.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) Public test labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c, function verify (CTest b05_depth.verify): PUSH, PUSH, ADD, HALT is accepted with peak 2; the program PUSH, BRANCH 4, PUSH, JUMP 4, PUSH, HALT, whose two paths reach PC 4 at different heights, returns B5_CONFLICT with peak left at 99 although neither path alone underflows; `JUMP 0` is accepted with peak 0; a program whose unreachable third record has opcode 99 returns B5_INVALID; a lone POP returns B5_CONFLICT. (c) A join-blind verifier (one that checks each path separately) is a learner-built variant; the B5_CONFLICT CHECK on the join program should reject it.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only by a join-blind verifier the learner builds (none is supplied; the public test b05_depth.verify only passes on a correct verifier): such a verifier falsely accepts a program with inconsistent heights, which breaks the verification property, but nothing executes it and no memory fault is produced, so it is not a sanitizer finding or proved impact.
security_lab.remediation: Propagate heights along every edge, reject differing joins with B5_CONFLICT and publish the peak only after acceptance; the existing test b05_depth.verify (the `join[]` CHECK `b5_verify(join, 6, &peak) == B5_CONFLICT && peak == 99` in labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c) must reject the learner-built join-blind variant.
security_lab.limitations: A passing verifier says nothing about termination (JUMP 0 loops forever), initialized values, the real CVM, native execution or exploitability; no flawed verifier is supplied, so the false accept is shown only on a variant the learner builds.

exercises.title: Committed-prefix recovery and hostile checksum evidence

environment.language: C17; explicitly labeled C23 comparison only
environment.target: Linux x86-64 hosted bounded model
environment.dependencies: Original mechanism uses type/limit headers; libc/Python/ctypes are host verification dependencies.

security_lab.target: labs/b05_depth/src/depth.c (b5_recover) over copied synthetic record arrays.
security_lab.adversary: Controls the fixture records: up to 8 records each with generation, value, XOR checksum and commit flag, including paired changes to generation and value that preserve the checksum, a flipped checksum bit, an uncommitted record and old generations. Does not control the trusted checkpoint, the recovery code or any real disk.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity and availability of recovered state: only the contiguous committed prefix after the checkpoint may be recovered, and because the XOR checksum is not authentication, a paired change of generation and value that preserves the checksum can make a newer committed record look like checkpointed history and be silently ignored.
security_lab.boundary: Hosted bounded model with copied in-memory arrays; no real storage, file system or crash is involved and crash cuts are enumerated, not caused.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) Public test labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c, function recover (CTest b05_depth.recover): with checkpoint (5,10) and valid records 6/12, 7/18, 8/23 the recovered value is the last committed value for each prefix length 0..3; flipping one checksum bit of record 1 returns B5_CONFLICT with out left at 99; clearing its commit flag stops at 12; a non-contiguous generation returns B5_CONFLICT. The weak-checksum case: a committed record {9,200} with checkpoint (8,100) recovers 200, but flipping the low bit of both its generation and value keeps `weak.checksum == b5_checksum(...)` and recovery now returns 100 with no error, so a committed update is silently dropped. The payload-durable, commit-durable and acknowledged crash-cut enumeration is a learner deliverable with no supplied harness.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, demonstrated by a supplied artifact: the weak case of the public test b05_depth.recover (labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c:58-66) pins recovery returning 100 for the paired change on any conforming b5_recover, so no learner-built variant is needed for this one; the crash-cut cases are learner-built. A checksum-preserving paired corruption silently discards a committed update in the model, showing the XOR checksum is not authentication, but it requires attacker control of both altered fields and affects only a synthetic array, so it is not a proved impact.
security_lab.remediation: State in the contract that the checksum detects accidental corruption only, keep rejecting single-field corruption and generation gaps, and treat a paired-change acceptance as outside the checksum's guarantee; the existing test b05_depth.recover (the `weak` checks in labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c, which record the original behaviour) must continue to document that case, and a stronger keyed check, if the learner adds one, must reject the paired change.
security_lab.limitations: The weak XOR checksum cannot become authentication within this lab, crash cuts are modelled rather than measured, the checkpoint is trusted, and no real file system or production recovery is examined.

exercises.title: Permission preflight across synthetic user pages

environment.language: C17; explicitly labeled C23 comparison only
environment.target: Linux x86-64 hosted bounded model
environment.dependencies: Original mechanism uses type/limit headers; libc/Python/ctypes are host verification dependencies.

security_lab.target: labs/b05_depth/src/depth.c (b5_copy_to_user) over a synthetic four-page memory array.
security_lab.adversary: Controls the numeric destination address, the byte count and the per-page permission flags of the synthetic pages, including page-crossing copies, count 0 with address 64, missing user or writable flags and overflowing lengths. Does not control the page-table owner, the source bytes' validity checks, the 64-byte backing array or any host privilege.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity under rejection: a copy that fails permission checking on any page must modify no byte of the destination, so a partial prefix must never be visible after a rejected request.
security_lab.boundary: Hosted bounded model with an original four-page, 64-byte array and no real page tables, kernel, privilege or host memory change.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) Public test labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c, function copy (CTest b05_depth.copy): with all four pages present, user and writable, copying 4 bytes at address 14 succeeds and writes input bytes 1..4 across the page-0/page-1 boundary; after clearing writable on page 1, copying 2 bytes at 15 returns B5_CONFLICT and p[0].bytes[15] keeps its old value; count 0 at address 64 succeeds, address 64 with count 1 and address SIZE_MAX with count 2 return B5_RANGE; clearing the user flag on page 1 makes a 1-byte copy at 16 return B5_CONFLICT. The public test compares only byte 15, so the all-64-byte equality snapshot is a check the learner adds. (c) The incremental-write mutant named in the brief is learner-built; it should fail the p[0].bytes[15] == old CHECK, and the full-array snapshot makes the leak complete.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only by the incremental-write mutant the learner builds (none is supplied; the public test b05_depth.copy only passes on a correct copy): the mutant exposes a modified prefix after rejection, which breaks the all-or-nothing property in the model, but no kernel or privilege boundary exists and nothing is escalated, so it is not a proved impact.
security_lab.remediation: Preflight every touched page's present, user and writable flags and check address plus count for overflow before the first write; the existing test b05_depth.copy (the `b5_copy_to_user(p, 15, input, 2) == B5_CONFLICT && p[0].bytes[15] == old` CHECK in labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c) must reject the learner-built incremental-write mutant, and the learner adds a whole-array equality regression.
security_lab.limitations: Shows an all-or-nothing property in a four-page model only, and no flawed copy is supplied, so the prefix leak is shown on a mutant the learner builds; it says nothing about real MMU behaviour, races between check and copy, or privilege escalation.

security_lab.adversary: Controls the order and generation of ACK events delivered to shoot_ack (a delayed CPU1 ACK, a stale ACK1 from the prior generation) and when reclaim is attempted; does not control the captured CPU set, the generation counter, or the synthetic frame labels OLD and NEW.
security_lab.violated_property: Memory-reuse safety (confidentiality/integrity of the recycled frame): a frame must not be reused for NEW while any captured CPU may still hold a translation to OLD.
security_lab.boundary: Local unprivileged host process over a finite model with synthetic OLD/NEW labels; no real page tables, IPIs, ISA invalidation or kernel; native claims need a separate disposable-guest QEMU adapter. Harmless success is a logical stale-view read of NEW.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `b045_systems.shoot` (labs/b045_systems/tests/tests.c, function shoot): after s_shoot_begin(&s,3) and the current-generation ACK from CPU0 it prints `shootdown observation: delayed CPU sees synthetic label 1` and requires `frame_label == 1 && reclaimed == S_PENDING && !s.reclaimed`, then `s_shoot_ack(&s, 1, gen - 1) == S_CONFLICT && s.pending == 2`, then current ACK1 and `!s_shoot_reclaim(&s) && s.reclaimed`. Learner-built early-reclaim variant (the Problem asks for it; D3 asks for mutant diagnosis): a reclaim that sets reclaimed while CPU1 is pending makes the test print `synthetic label 2` and exit 1 with `DEPTH_CHECK:<line>:frame_label == 1 && reclaimed == S_PENDING && !s.reclaimed`; a variant that ignores the generation fails the `gen - 1` CHECK.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only by the learner-built early-reclaim variant (none is supplied): the supplied test on a correct build prints only the OLD view (`synthetic label 1`) and passes, so a stale view observing NEW (`synthetic label 2`) appears only when a variant you build reclaims early. It is not proved-impact because no real translation cache, privilege boundary or exploit exists.
security_lab.remediation: Snapshot the target mask at begin, clear a pending bit only for an ACK carrying the current generation, and refuse reclaim until the mask is empty; the regression is the existing CTest `b045_systems.shoot` (run as `depth-tests shoot`), which must reject both learner-built variants with the DEPTH_CHECK lines above.
security_lab.limitations: Shows a logical label in a finite model only: no real TLB, barrier, IPI or CPU hot-unplug behaviour (the hot-unplug quiescence handshake is variant V2, not in the supplied test); the host function trusts ACK meaning, and one fixed history is not a proof over all schedules.

security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `b045_systems.peer` (labs/b045_systems/tests/tests.c, function peer) requires, in order: `s_peer_restart(&p, 0) == S_PENDING && p.outstanding` (untrusted restart keeps work), `!s_peer_restart(&p, 1) && p.epoch == 2 && p.uncertain && !p.outstanding && !p.ready`, `s_peer_ready(&p, 1) == S_CONFLICT`, a resubmit with `seq == 1`, then `s_peer_ack(&p, 1, 1) == S_CONFLICT && p.outstanding` (stale epoch), `!s_peer_ack(&p, 2, 1) && !p.outstanding`, a repeated ACK returning S_CONFLICT, and at epoch UINT32_MAX `s_peer_restart(&p, 1) == S_CONFLICT`. security_lab.violated_property: Lifetime safety: the descriptor and buffer must stay owned until trusted completion, so cancellation must not permit reap and reuse while the device may still complete the old request.

security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `b05_depth.request` (labs/b05_depth/tests/tests.c, function request) requires: after submit and cancel `r.state == B5_CANCEL_REQUESTED && !r.terminal_count`; `b5_request(&r, B5_REAP, 1, 0) == B5_CONFLICT` while cancel is pending; completion then wins with `r.terminal_count == 1`; a second completion `b5_request(&r, B5_COMPLETE, 1, 1) == B5_CONFLICT && r.result == 2`; reap then gives `r.generation == 2`; a generation-1 completion afterwards is B5_CONFLICT; and at UINT32_MAX reap gives `r.state == B5_RETIRED`. security_lab.adversary: Chooses the input span and length (for example the 130-byte sequence), the injected allocation failure point fail_after=0,1,2, clone and thread counts and the kind field; cannot write frame ownership counts or the backing array directly.
security_lab.violated_property: Resource integrity and isolation: a failed load must leak no owned frame, a COW write to the child must not alter the parent, and rejected requests must modify no earlier page.
security_lab.boundary: Local process with 16 synthetic frames (reference counts plus 16 arrays of 64 bytes in one struct) and bounded inputs; the test forks nothing, creates no files and opens no sockets or devices, and prints only to standard output and error; disposable VM only for kernel transfer; harmless success is a leaked frame count or a changed parent byte.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `service_depth.memory` (labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c, function memory) requires, for fail_after 0,1,2, `sd_load(...) == SD_FULL && a.length == 99` and `m.refs[i] == 0` for all 16 frames (no leaked reference); after a good load `a.count == 3 && m.bytes[a.frames[2]][1] == 130 && m.bytes[a.frames[2]][2] == 0`; `sd_clone(...,2,...) == SD_INVALID` and a DENIED clone leaves the image bytes identical (memcmp); a denied-allocation child write `sd_write(&m,&b,0,99,0) == SD_FULL && m.bytes[a.frames[0]][0] == 1`; the allowed write gives parent byte 1 and child byte 99 on distinct frames; and with four loaded images `sd_load(...) == SD_FULL` leaves every `m.refs[i] == 1`. The shared contract (labs/service_depth/CONTRACTS.md, Local security scope) names a leaked frame count as the harmless success condition. The variants are yours to build: one in which a failed load leaves frames owned, and one in which a write through the clone can be seen in the parent's frame; record the SD_CHECK line each one reaches. The assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once you build a flawed variant: no supplied artifact leaks a frame or changes a parent byte, so the evidence is your variant's failing SD_CHECK line. A wrong ownership count or parent byte is observed, but a crash or UB here would only be a crash or undefined-behaviour class, and no arbitrary execution or privilege escalation is shown.
security_lab.remediation: Preflight every allocation before publishing the image, share frames with reference counts and copy on write, and validate kind and thread count before touching any page; the regression is the existing CTest `service_depth.memory` (`service_depth-tests memory`), which must reject each of your variants.
security_lab.limitations: Only the 16-frame struct sd_memory model is exercised: no real page tables, TLB, concurrent fork or memory pressure; the kernel adapter deliverable is derived on paper, and lifetime, trusted-capability and stable-copy assumptions are the caller's.

security_lab.target: labs/service_depth: sd_channel_init/sd_grant/sd_send/sd_receive/sd_channel_close/sd_channel_reopen (src/service_depth.c, include/) as exercised by the channel case of labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c and fixtures/service_depth/X-T56-003.json.
security_lab.adversary: Chooses message bytes {1,0,255}, which capability (SEND-only or old pre-reopen) is presented, destination size and a validator that denies the span; cannot forge RECEIVE rights, edit the epoch or write protected channel metadata.
security_lab.violated_property: Authorization and transactionality: bytes must not be delivered without RECEIVE permission, a failed receive must consume nothing, and a capability from a closed epoch must be rejected after reopen.
security_lab.boundary: Local process with a two-slot in-memory queue of messages up to 32 bytes, synthetic bytes and a destination buffer pre-filled with the canary 77; the test forks nothing, creates no files and opens no sockets or devices, and prints only to standard output and error; disposable VM only for kernel transfer; harmless success is a byte received without RECEIVE right.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `service_depth.channel` (labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c, function channel) requires: receive through the SEND-only capability `== SD_DENIED && q.count == 1 && n == 99`; a validator that denies the span `== SD_COPY && q.count == 1 && n == 99 && out[0] == 77` (canary intact); a 2-byte destination `== SD_FULL && q.count == 1`; `sd_grant` of rights 3 from the RECEIVE-only capability `== SD_DENIED` (no amplification); after close, send is SD_CLOSED, the exact bytes {1,0,255} drain with `n == 3`, then receive is SD_CLOSED; after reopen the old capability gives `sd_send == SD_STALE`; zero-length NULL send/receive are SD_OK; and at epoch UINT32_MAX `sd_channel_reopen == SD_FULL && q.retired`. The shared contract names a byte received without RECEIVE permission as the harmless success condition. The variants are yours to build: one in which a capability without RECEIVE rights can still take a message, and one in which a refused receive still shortens the queue; record the SD_CHECK line each one reaches. The assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once you build a flawed variant: no supplied artifact delivers a byte without permission or loses a message, so the evidence is your variant's failing SD_CHECK line. A byte is delivered without permission or a message is lost, but a crash or UB would be only a crash or undefined-behaviour class, and no privilege escalation or arbitrary write is shown.
security_lab.remediation: Check rights, destination size and span validation before dequeuing, copy then commit, bump the epoch on close and retire at UINT32_MAX; the regression is the existing CTest `service_depth.channel` (`service_depth-tests channel`), which must reject each of your variants.
security_lab.limitations: Only the two-slot struct sd_channel model with a callback validator: it does not show real user-copy races, page faults or concurrency, and a callback that checks a transient page table does not provide the stable copyout proof the Problem asks you to derive.

security_lab.target: labs/service_depth: sd_files_init/sd_open/sd_dup/sd_seek/sd_read/sd_close (src/service_depth.c, include/) as exercised by the files case of labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c and fixtures/service_depth/X-T56-004.json.
security_lab.adversary: Chooses open names (including ../alpha and duplicates), seek offsets (negative, out of range), read lengths, the denied-read injection, stale handle closes and handle exhaustion; cannot modify the borrowed archive bytes or the description table directly.
security_lab.violated_property: State integrity and bounds: duplicated handles must share one offset, a denied read must not advance it, reads must stay within the entry, and archive bytes must stay live until the last description closes.
security_lab.boundary: Local process over a 10-byte synthetic entry and an empty entry; no real filesystem, paths or syscalls; disposable VM only for kernel transfer; harmless success is a wrong offset or extra byte returned.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `service_depth.files` (labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c, function files) requires reads of 3 and 4 on independent opens to give "012" and "0123"; reading 2 through the duplicate gives "34" and 1 through the original gives '5'; a read whose validator denies the copy `== SD_COPY && n == 99` and the next read still yields '6' (offset unchanged); after seek to end-1 a 3-byte read gives `n == 1 && out[0] == '9'`; `sd_seek(...,0,-1) == SD_INVALID`; a repeated close is SD_STALE; `sd_open("../alpha") == SD_INVALID`; duplicate names and zero entries make sd_files_init SD_INVALID with the table unchanged; handle exhaustion is SD_FULL and exhausted generations never reissue a handle. The shared contract names a changed offset after a rejected copy as the harmless success condition. Learner-built variants: advancing the offset before the copy fails the '6' CHECK after the denied read; giving each duplicate a private offset fails the "34" CHECK.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in the learner-built early-advance and private-offset variants (none is supplied; the supplied test service_depth.files passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): a specific wrong offset or returned byte is then observed, but it is not a sanitizer-finding or proved-impact since the archive is a small synthetic array and no escape to real files occurs.
security_lab.remediation: Share one description among duplicates, advance the offset only after a successful copy, validate names and seeks, clamp reads to the entry and never reissue exhausted generations; the regression is the existing CTest `service_depth.files` (`service_depth-tests files`), which must reject the early-advance and private-offset variants.
security_lab.limitations: Only an in-memory table of two synthetic entries: no real filesystem, path resolution, concurrent offset race or kernel file table is exercised, and liveness of the borrowed archive bytes is a caller discipline the test does not enforce.

security_lab.target: labs/service_depth: sd_apply/sd_recover over struct sd_journal (src/service_depth.c, include/) as exercised by the journal case of labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c and fixtures/service_depth/X-T56-005.json.
security_lab.adversary: Chooses operation IDs and deltas (ID1 delta7, ID1 delta8, ID2 delta-3, near-overflow deltas), the fault cut 1..4 within the atomic-flush model, and may flip a committed payload byte; cannot write commit markers or recompute a valid checksum in the guaranteed profile.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity and exactly-once effect: a retried operation must not apply its delta twice, an uncertain fault must not be reported as success, and a corrupted committed payload must be detected.
security_lab.boundary: Local process with a synthetic counter and a modelled journal held in two 32-byte durable and two 32-byte pending arrays inside one struct; the test forks nothing, creates no files and opens no sockets or devices, and prints only to standard output and error, so no real storage, power loss or disk is involved; harmless success is a doubled or falsely acknowledged local integer effect.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test `service_depth.journal` (labs/service_depth/tests/tests.c, function journal) requires, for fault 1..4, `sd_apply(&j,1,7,fault,&out) == SD_UNCERTAIN && out == 99`, recovery `r.last == (fault == 4 ? 1u : 0u)` with `r.value == (fault == 4 ? 7 : 0)`, then retry `sd_apply(&j,1,7,0,&out) == 0 && out == 7`, ID1 delta 8 `== SD_CONFLICT && out == 7`, ID2 delta -3 `out == 4` and old ID1 `== SD_STALE`; `sd_apply(&j,2,1,0,&out) == SD_FULL && out == INT32_MAX` after an INT32_MAX delta; after `j.durable[1][12] ^= 1` recovery returns `SD_CORRUPT` with `r.last == 99`; and the alternating-slot loop with IDs 1..3 and `out == 123` preserved. The shared contract names a falsely acknowledged or doubled local integer effect as the harmless success condition. The variants are yours to build: one in which a retry of an operation whose commit was already durable applies its effect a second time, and one that reports success for a cut at which recovery would not find the operation committed; record the SD_CHECK line each one reaches. The assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once you build a flawed variant: no supplied artifact doubles or falsely acknowledges an effect, so the evidence is your variant's failing SD_CHECK line. A doubled or falsely acknowledged integer effect is observed, but it is not proved-impact because the journal is a model and no real data loss or privilege change occurs.
security_lab.remediation: Write the full record and its checksum before acknowledging, answer duplicates from the stored receipt, reject signed overflow before mutating the journal and make recovery deterministic; the regression is the existing CTest `service_depth.journal` (`service_depth-tests journal`), which must reject each of your variants.
security_lab.limitations: A checksum detects accidents, not tampering: changing a commit marker or recomputing a checksum is outside the guarantee and is not tested; the atomic-flush model is a simulation of cuts 1..4, not real storage or power loss; the file-channel-journal composition (labs/service_depth/tests/composition.c) is a separate check.

security_lab.adversary: Controls the mode, the counter in 0..100, the amount in -100..100 and the starting report count (including SIZE_MAX), plus invalid modes and null objects; does not control the predicate or the report counter except through er_contract_counter.
security_lab.violated_property: Contract and state integrity: in ENFORCE a violating update must not change the counter, a report must be counted exactly once per observed violation, and report-count exhaustion must not wrap or change state.
security_lab.boundary: Local unprivileged process with synthetic caller-owned integers; candidate sum cannot overflow on any supported int; no code-execution claim; harmless success is an out-of-range counter or lost report.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied tests: `errors.contracts` (labs/errors/tests/tests.c) requires `er_contract_counter(ER_ENFORCE, 20, &value, &reports) == ER_CONTRACT && value == 90 && reports == 1`, then ER_OBSERVE `== ER_OK && value == 100 && reports == 2`, then ER_OFF `== ER_OK && value == 100 && reports == 2` (no new report), and with `reports = SIZE_MAX` ENFORCE returns ER_RANGE with value 90 and reports SIZE_MAX unchanged; `errors.modes_base` (labs/errors/contract_modes/tests/tests.c) repeats these and requires ER_OBSERVE amount 1 at SIZE_MAX reports to be `ER_RANGE && c == 100 && r == SIZE_MAX`. The Problem names the two learner-built variants: a missing-report variant (OBSERVE does not count) and an enforce-still-commits variant (ENFORCE changes the counter to 100); the first fails the `reports == 2` CHECK and the second fails `value == 90 && reports == 1`.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in the two learner-built variants (none is supplied; the supplied tests errors.contracts and errors.modes_base pass on a correct build and so demonstrate no violation): a specific wrong counter or report count is then observed, but it is not proved-impact because only a local synthetic integer changes and no exploit or privilege effect follows.
security_lab.remediation: Compute the candidate sum, apply the predicate per mode, check report capacity before changing either object and keep the counter unchanged in ENFORCE; the regressions are the existing CTests `errors.contracts` and `errors.modes_base`, which must reject the missing-report and enforce-still-commits variants.
security_lab.limitations: An original local state-integrity experiment on caller-owned integers, not a general safe unchecked-call API; the ER_INVALID rows and the all-inputs enumeration against an integer model are separate deliverables, and concurrent use needs the external serialization described in labs/errors/contract_modes/MODES.md.

security_lab.target: labs/ownership (src/ownership.c: ow_flawed_write and ow_checked_write on OwTenantArena, plus labs/ownership/authority_boundary for the serialized request path)
security_lab.adversary: Controls the numeric tenant, offset, count (count<=8) and value of tenant0 write requests, including offsets near UINT_MAX; has no arbitrary pointer, no control of the arena layout, no privileges and no second process.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of tenant isolation: a request authorized only for tenant0 indices 0..7 changes tenant1 indices 8..15 because the wrapped sum offset+count passes the extent check.
security_lab.boundary: Local hosted process, one synthetic int32_t[16] arena with canary 99 in tenant1, bounded to one call per case; harmless success is the canary changing from 99 to 7; every physical access stays inside the 16-element array.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test ownership.facade (labs/ownership/tests/tests.c, function facade) asserts: ow_flawed_write(&a,0,UINT_MAX-3u,8,7)==OW_OK and a.data[12]==7 where tenant1 held 99; ow_checked_write with the same arguments returns OW_INVALID and all 16 elements still equal the initial pattern; (8,0) is OW_OK, (8,1) is OW_INVALID, and tenant1 (7,1) is OK and (7,2) INVALID. Supplied test ownership.authority_defect (labs/ownership/authority_boundary/tests/tests.c) additionally asserts the flawed call sets indices 0..3 and 12..15 to 7 and leaves 4..11 alone, and ownership.authority_bounds enumerates tenant/offset/count combinations. D3 asks the learner to build a sanitizer run and a flawed-check variant that ownership.facade must reject by a CHECK, and to explain why ASan can stay quiet; those are learner-built, not supplied.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, demonstrated by a supplied artifact: the supplied ow_flawed_write (labs/ownership/src/ownership.c:260) is called by the supplied tests ownership.facade (tests/tests.c:337) and ownership.authority_defect (authority_boundary/tests/tests.c:53), so no learner-built variant is needed to see the canary change (only the sanitizer run and the flawed-check variant of D3 are learner-built): a semantic assertion on the tenant1 canary shows the isolation invariant broken; it is not undefined-behaviour or a sanitizer finding because unsigned wrap is defined and no access leaves the array, and it is not proved-impact because no code execution or privilege change is shown.
security_lab.remediation: Subtraction-based checks (tenant<=1, offset<=8, count<=8-offset) before trusted indexing with all 16 elements unchanged on failure; the regression that rejects the original input is ownership.facade (the UINT_MAX-3, count 8 case and the offset 8/count 0 edge) together with ownership.authority_defect and ownership.authority_bounds.
security_lab.limitations: Does not show out-of-bounds C access, code execution or escalation; relies on the declared 32-bit unsigned width and masking model; same-process arbitrary writes and forged native pointers are outside the façade guarantee; the serialized-request investigation is a separate assessed extension.

security_lab.adversary: Chooses which issue, attenuate, add, read and revoke requests are submitted, the requested rights mask (0..3), the owner identity presented and which retired capability copy is replayed; in the forgery variant a same-process C client may overwrite exposed capability fields; it cannot change the authority record in the broker process.
security_lab.violated_property: Authorization and integrity of the synthetic counter: a capability must never hold more rights than its parent, add requires both root and capability permission, an old epoch must be stale after revocation, and a capability must not act for another owner.
security_lab.boundary: Local cooperative model over one synthetic int counter and, for the broker part, the original forked child; bounded finite epochs (retire after 3); harmless success is the counter changing contrary to policy, never a crash or an OS privilege change.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test dispatch.capabilities (labs/dispatch/tests/tests.c, case capabilities) asserts: a read-only attenuation ds_cap_add returns DS_DENIED with root.counter==0; ds_cap_attenuate(read,3) returns DS_DENIED with rights still 1; the full capability adds 5 (counter 5); after ds_cap_revoke the old full capability returns DS_STALE with counter still 5. Supplied test dispatch.broker (labs/dispatch/tests/broker.c, function checks) asserts derive beyond held rights returns DS_DENIED, derive with a full grant table DS_FULL, revoke to epoch 4 then DS_FULL, stale replies after revoke, a duplicate sequence returns DS_STALE with the counter unchanged, and a malformed request returns DS_INVALID without consuming the sequence. The owner-crossing attempt and the direct forgery of exposed ds_capability fields (rights, epoch, owner) are learner-built clients the brief asks for; the counter change they cause is the evidence, and dispatch.capabilities is not expected to reject a forged struct.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only by the learner-built forged-field and owner-crossing clients (the supplied dispatch.capabilities and dispatch.broker tests assert that the API denies, so they demonstrate no violation, and no forging client is supplied): the forged-field client changes the synthetic counter contrary to the rights policy, which refutes any claim beyond cooperative callers; not undefined-behaviour or a sanitizer-finding because the writes are ordinary valid C, and not proved-impact because no real credential or privilege is affected.
security_lab.remediation: Subset check on attenuation, epoch check and both-rights check on add, state unchanged on rejection; the regression that rejects the original input is dispatch.capabilities (stronger mask, revoked reuse) plus dispatch.broker (derive denial, stale sequence); the learner adds a cross-owner case to dispatch.capabilities. The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: Checked API transitions are enforceable only while callers use the API; a C client that writes exposed fields, or any same-process arbitrary write, defeats the model and refutes a broader security claim; the broker narrows this only under its fixed holder and grant model, with new obligations (authentication, replay, handle lifetime) it does not fully solve.

security_lab.target: labs/protocols (src/protocols.c: pt_session_step for client and server roles, with the in-process two-endpoint trace driver)
security_lab.adversary: Chooses the sequence of (sending role, message tag) pairs presented to the session, including wrong direction, wrong tag, replay of an earlier message and any message after the terminal state; cannot alter the phase table or drop transport messages undetected.
security_lab.violated_property: Protocol integrity: each endpoint may advance only on the tag and direction its current phase allows, the remaining count must fall exactly once per ACK, and a terminal session must never make progress again.
security_lab.boundary: Local in-process trace with synthetic messages and two endpoint structures; finite phase table, so enumeration is bounded; no network, no external service.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test protocols.session (labs/protocols/tests/tests.c, function session) enumerates both roles and remaining 0..8 and asserts: a step from the wrong side (pt_session_step(&s, role, PT_HELLO)) returns PT_STATE with phase 0; HELLO then ACCEPT proceed; each DATA/ACK pair keeps phase and decreases remaining by exactly one; BYE reaches phase 5 and a second BYE returns PT_STATE. A wrong-tag case and a defective variant the learner builds (for example skipping the direction check), recorded as the shared security contract in labs/protocols/CONTRACTS.md asks, must be rejected by protocols.session; neither is supplied.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a learner-built defective variant (none is supplied; the supplied test protocols.session passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): an illegal transition recorded by the trace is the observable; not undefined-behaviour or sanitizer-finding since all accesses are valid, and not proved-impact since it affects only a synthetic automaton.
security_lab.remediation: Reject any step whose direction or tag the phase table does not admit before changing state and keep BYE absorbing; the regression that rejects the original input is protocols.session (wrong direction, terminal reuse), plus the learner-added wrong-tag case. The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: Matching automata still deadlock if a message is dropped or an endpoint is never scheduled; C tags and runtime checks do not inherit the guarantees of a typed session language; the delayed simultaneous close and cancel case is separate.

security_lab.adversary: Chooses the sequence of posted events, the number of posts into a full ring and a scripted failure of trace output capacity during dispatch; cannot forge event pointers, change ring storage or alter trusted quiescence facts.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity and availability of queued work: a full ring must reject without overwriting or reordering a queued event, and an event whose dispatch fails must be retained rather than lost, with head, count and active state unchanged.
security_lab.boundary: Local in-process model with four copied event values, synthetic events and a bounded trace buffer; no interrupt or scheduler hardware, no external input.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test protocols.active (labs/protocols/tests/tests.c, function active) asserts: stepping an empty queue returns PT_PENDING leaving the output count 9; four pt_post calls succeed and the fifth returns PT_RANGE with count 4 and queue[0]==PT_CONNECT; pt_active_step with trace capacity 1 returns PT_RANGE with count 4, head 0 and machine OFFLINE; four steps with capacity 6 then succeed, leaving count 0 and active==PT_FAULT. A defective overwrite or remove-before-dispatch variant, as the labs/protocols/CONTRACTS.md security paragraph asks, is learner-built and must be rejected by protocols.active.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a learner-built overwrite or remove-before-dispatch variant (none is supplied; the supplied test protocols.active passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): a lost or overwritten queued event is then observable by a synthetic counter or FIFO oracle; not undefined-behaviour or sanitizer-finding because the ring is copied values with valid indices, and not proved-impact because only synthetic events are affected.
security_lab.remediation: Reject posting at capacity and remove an event only after its dispatch succeeded; the regression that rejects the original input is protocols.active (fifth post, trace-capacity failure and retry). The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: Rejection preserves FIFO but gives no fairness under sustained load, and retention exposes a poison-event policy; the ISR and scheduler adapter is not exercised by the host model.

security_lab.target: labs/protocols (src/protocols.c: pt_driver_start, pt_driver_complete and pt_driver_recover over the original register and DMA port model)
security_lab.adversary: Controls the timing and outcome of the scripted fake port: start failure, completion with the device still active (quiet 0), completion before or after quiescence and repeated completion; cannot change trusted quiescence facts, forge buffer pointers or touch hardware.
security_lab.violated_property: Ownership and liveness integrity: a buffer lent to DMA must be retained until quiescence is proved, a failed start must leave RecoveryRequired with the same borrowed pointer, and a non-quiescent completion must not release the buffer or feed the watchdog.
security_lab.boundary: Local host model with a synthetic register and DMA port; no board, no flashing, no real peripheral; harmless success is a premature release or watchdog event recorded by a counter.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test protocols.driver (labs/protocols/tests/tests.c, function driver) asserts: with port.fail set, pt_driver_start returns PT_RECOVERY, state PT_RECOVERY_REQUIRED, dma_owned set and d.buffer==b==port.borrow; pt_driver_recover returns PT_PENDING while the port is not quiet and still owns the buffer; once port.quiet is set it returns 0 with !dma_owned, !port.borrow and PT_CLOSED; after a good start, pt_driver_complete(&d,0,0) returns PT_PENDING with dma_owned and port.watch==0; (0,1) returns 0, releases the buffer and sets port.watch==1; a repeated completion returns PT_STATE with port.watch still 1. A defective early-release variant is learner-built (labs/protocols/CONTRACTS.md security paragraph) and must be rejected by protocols.driver.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a learner-built early-release variant (none is supplied; the supplied test protocols.driver passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): a premature buffer release or a watchdog fed while DMA may still run would then be observed through counters; not undefined-behaviour or sanitizer-finding because the fake port never writes the buffer, and not proved-impact because no real DMA corruption occurs.
security_lab.remediation: Retain the buffer until the port reports quiescence, leave recovery as the only exit from PT_RECOVERY_REQUIRED, and feed the watchdog only on normal completion; the regression that rejects the original input is protocols.driver (failed start, quiet 0 completion, repeated completion). The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: Register ordering, cache maintenance and interrupt serialization of a real firmware adapter are not modelled; a late completion from a previous boot needs epoch validation not covered here; no physical DMA behaviour is shown.

security_lab.target: labs/coroutines (src/coroutines.c: co_parse over the bounded struct co_parser DAG with CO_LITERAL, CO_EMPTY, CO_SEQUENCE, CO_CHOICE and CO_MANY)
security_lab.adversary: Chooses the input bytes, the grammar DAG within the bounded node count (including many applied to a nullable parser) and the visit budget; cannot supply unbounded grammars, mutate the DAG during a parse or inject callbacks.
security_lab.violated_property: Availability and parse integrity: a parse must terminate within the visit budget, a nullable repetition must be rejected rather than loop without progress, and a failed alternative must roll the cursor back so the wrong prefix is not accepted.
security_lab.boundary: Local process, immutable bounded DAG (recursion depth at most 16), fixed small inputs and a finite budget; the harmless success is a non-terminating or over-budget visit count caught by the budget, or a wrong acceptance, never a hang left running.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test coroutines.parser (labs/coroutines/tests/tests.c, function parser) asserts: on the choice(sequence(a,b),a) DAG, co_parse of `ac` returns 0 with end 1 and of `ab` end 2; `x` returns CO_NO_MATCH with end left at 91; a zero budget with no input returns CO_RANGE with end 91 and steps==0; a many over an empty node returns CO_STATE with end 91. A defective variant without the progress check or without cursor rollback is learner-built (labs/coroutines/CONTRACTS.md security paragraph) and must be rejected by coroutines.parser; run it only with a finite visit budget.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a learner-built variant without the progress check or cursor rollback (none is supplied; the supplied test coroutines.parser passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): a budget exhaustion or wrong accepted end is then recorded as a failing semantic assertion; not undefined-behaviour or sanitizer-finding since the budget bounds the work, and not proved-impact because it demonstrates a bounded denial-of-progress in a teaching parser only.
security_lab.remediation: Reject nullable repetition, charge visits against the budget and restore the cursor on a failed branch; the regression that rejects the original input is coroutines.parser (the ac/ab/x inputs, budget 0 and the many-over-empty case). The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: Rollback applies to the cursor only, not to semantic side effects such as allocations; the work bound covers this grammar class, not arbitrary parsers; delayed action-allocation rollback is a separate case.

security_lab.adversary: Chooses the input string (length up to the cell capacity, with repeated a prefix, x and b or c suffix), the memo table size and whether cells are reused for a different input; cannot alter the grammar or the evaluation order.
security_lab.violated_property: Correctness and bounded work: a memoized result must be keyed by position and nonterminal and agree with the unmemoized grammar, failures must be cached too, and a mismatch must not modify the caller's output end.
security_lab.boundary: Local process, caller-owned fixed memo cells, inputs of at most a few dozen bytes; the harmless success is a wrong accept or an evaluation count above the bound, never unbounded runtime.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test coroutines.packrat (labs/coroutines/tests/tests.c, function packrat) asserts: co_packrat of `aaxcc` returns 0 with end 5 and calls==3; twelve a, x and twelve c return 0 with end 25 and calls==13; `aac` returns CO_NO_MATCH with end left at 91 and calls<=4; a memo table of 25 cells for the 25-byte input returns CO_INVALID with end 91. A variant without memoized failures or without reinitialized cells is learner-built (labs/coroutines/CONTRACTS.md security paragraph) and must be rejected by coroutines.packrat; reuse of a table across edited input is the learner's extension.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a learner-built variant without memoized failures or reinitialized cells (none is supplied; the supplied test coroutines.packrat passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): an excess cell count or wrong acceptance is then an observable property violation; not undefined-behaviour or sanitizer-finding since all cells are caller-owned and in range, and not proved-impact because it shows a bounded work or correctness defect in a teaching parser.
security_lab.remediation: Cache success and failure by position and nonterminal, reinitialize cells for each input and leave end untouched on failure; the regression that rejects the original input is coroutines.packrat (the three inputs and the undersized-table case). The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: The bound comes from the fixed grammar and per-cell actions; memo tables cost space proportional to input; a stale table after an edit is a separate delayed case; no claim about general PEG parsers.

security_lab.violated_property: Liveness and isolation of asynchronous progress: a readiness notification must not be lost between the first read and registration, a stale-generation notification must not mark a later frame ready, and a completed or cancelled frame must not publish or repeat output.
security_lab.boundary: Local serialized model with a synthetic reader and port, wanted length 1..8, at most two reads per poll; harmless success is a lost wakeup (frame never completes) or a stale notification flipping the next frame, observed by counters.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Supplied test coroutines.async (labs/coroutines/tests/tests.c, function async) asserts: co_async_poll of a 3-byte frame returns CO_DONE with n==3 and a.reads==2, a.arms==1, a.disarms==1; a second poll returns CO_DONE with reads still 2; in the second mode a poll returns CO_PENDING for generation 8, co_async_notify with stale generation 7 returns CO_STATE and with 8 returns 0; co_async_cancel returns 0 with disarms==1 and !registered; polling afterwards returns CO_STATE with reads unchanged. A variant without the recheck or the generation test is learner-built (labs/coroutines/CONTRACTS.md security paragraph) and must be rejected by coroutines.async.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only in a learner-built variant without the recheck or generation test (none is supplied; the supplied test coroutines.async passes on a correct build and so demonstrates no violation): a lost wakeup or wrongly ready frame is then a recorded counter and state mismatch; not undefined-behaviour or sanitizer-finding since reads stay within capacity, and not proved-impact because only a synthetic frame is affected.
security_lab.remediation: Arm and recheck within the same poll, compare generation on every notification, reject terminal frames and disarm synchronously; the regression that rejects the original input is coroutines.async (arm-then-recheck counters, stale notification, cancel then poll). The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.limitations: The recheck is sound only under the documented registration contract and synchronous disarm; the read callback's own bound cannot be repaired by checking the returned count; partial progress with error requires a no-retry policy not shown here; the generation must not be recycled while stale references remain.

security_lab.target: labs/coroutines (include/coroutines.h and src/coroutines.c, the COEffect start/resume/abort subset), exercised by the coroutines.effect CTest and fixtures/coroutines/PR-T72-09.json; your own implementation of the same contract is the attacked component.
security_lab.adversary: Controls the handler: the sequence of start/resume/abort calls, the two answer values (including a second answer that overflows the checked addition), and any saved copy of a continuation token (owner address plus generation). Does not control the library source, the frame's memory, the allocator or the host, and cannot forge a valid C pointer.
security_lab.violated_property: Single-shot resumption integrity: a continuation token must be consumed exactly once, so a stale or copied token must never be admitted a second time, the first answer must never be dropped or replayed, and a rejected overflowing second answer must leave frame, token and output unchanged.
security_lab.boundary: One local hosted-Linux process, a fresh live frame per case, synthetic uint32 answers, and learner-built flawed variants (replay admission, dropped first answer) that the Verification section requires you to reject; no stack switching, no external service, and the supplied build itself is never made vulnerable.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Backed by labs/coroutines/tests/tests.c function effect (CTest coroutines.effect): copying the question1 token as stale and resuming it after the first resume must return CO_STATE with the output still 91; answers 12 then 30 must return CO_DONE with output 42 and a consumed owner; start then abort must give pc 4 and a consumed token. A learner-built replay-admission variant (D3) must fail the stale CO_STATE check, and a dropped-first-answer variant must fail the 42 check. The overflow-then-retry and completed-reuse cases are learner-added tests required by D3 (the shared contract specifies unchanged token, frame and output on overflow), not part of the supplied effect test.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation: only against learner-built flawed variants, a duplicate or wrong result is an observable broken single-shot property on synthetic values; it is not proved-impact because no confidentiality, authorization or memory-safety consequence is shown, and not a crash, sanitizer finding or undefined behaviour because no fault occurs.
security_lab.remediation: Check owner address and generation on every resume and abort, advance the generation on consumption, and perform the checked addition before mutating anything. The existing regression is CTest coroutines.effect (function effect in labs/coroutines/tests/tests.c), whose stale-token CHECK rejects the original replayed input; add the overflow-then-retry test that D3 requires.
security_lab.limitations: Tokens are plain C structs, so copying, dangling frames and reinitialization ABA cannot be prevented by the library and are analysed, not executed; the demonstration says nothing about multi-shot control capture, native-stack continuations, concurrency or Koka equivalence, and bounded enumeration does not cover all executions.

security_lab.adversary: The attacker chooses the synthetic object graph (up to 16 identities, 4 ephemeron pairs, 4 weak references), the external-root set, the order of pair registration, the finalizer and resource flags on each new object, the callback behaviour (allocate, fail, resurrect by rooting the object) and the fail=1 injection schedule. The attacker does not control the collector's private state, forge handles or function pointers, or reenter the owner from outside the documented callback.
security_lab.violated_property: Modelled heap/lifetime integrity of the collector (handles are slot-and-generation indices into a fixed object array, not real memory): a value reachable only through an unreachable key (for example pair 4->5 whose value 5 points back to key 4) must be reclaimed, a chain such as pairs 2->3 then 1->2 with root 1 must keep all three, a weak reference must clear before finalizer retention, and each identity must finalize at most once with its synthetic resource released exactly once.
security_lab.boundary: Single-process, single-threaded runs on the synthetic owner (16 identities, 4 ephemeron pairs, 4 weak references, 16 pending finalizers, 48 admitted identities over the owner lifetime), built with the GCC/Clang Debug, Release and ASan/UBSan profiles. The object_runtime.weak, object_runtime.ephemeron_graph and object_runtime.finalizers binaries start no thread or child process and open no file or socket; they write only to stdout and stderr. Success is a wrong live set, callback count or resource count on synthetic objects; no real resource or other principal exists.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) CTest object_runtime.weak (labs/object_runtime/tests/tests.c, weak): with pairs 2->3 and 1->2 under root 1 and a value-to-key edge on 4/5, CHECK(or_weak_collect(&h,&dead)==OR_OK && dead==24 && h.graph.live==7 && h.weak[0]==0), then a queued object gives pending==1, a second collect returns OR_STATE, or_final_next sets finalized==1, and later rooting and unrooting reclaims (dead==3). (a) object_runtime.ephemeron_graph (tests/finalizers_ext.c, ephemeron): the chain a[2]->a[3], a[0]->a[1] keeps live==15 with dead==0, and after unrooting a[0] with edge a[3]->a[0] the check requires dead==15 and live==0 with all key/value slots cleared. (a) object_runtime.finalizers (finalizers): calls==0 before any collection, collect with pending finalizers returns OR_STATE unchanged, one orf_run_one gives calls==1 and finalized==1, cleanup budgets 0, 1, 5 and 99 release resources exactly once, orf_close releases with calls==0, and a resurrecting callback leaves graph.roots==2 until a later collection. The oracle mode of the same driver (`object-runtime-finalizers oracle`, tests/finalizers_ext.c:247-287) is not a registered CTest and compares nothing: it enumerates 64 strong graphs x 16 root sets x 25 conditional targets (5 x 5) = 25,600 cases and prints one row 'F graph mask v0 v1 live dead' per case, where live and dead are 16-bit masks. fixtures/object_runtime/finalizers_ext.json holds no expected rows (only the row count, the input dimensions, a two-step delayed trace and case names), so the learner writes an independent model of strong plus conditional reachability and compares all 25,600 rows against it. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own implementation, each stated as a property to break: a collector in which a pair's value is lost although its key is reachable through an earlier pair's value (the reverse-ordered chain then reports a live mask short of 15 at tests/finalizers_ext.c:233-234), and a finalizer driver in which one identity can be finalized twice (tests/finalizers_ext.c:112-113 checks calls==1 and finalized==1 after the first orf_run_one, so it catches only a variant that never sets the finalized bit or runs the callback more than once in that call; a real finalize-twice variant passes there and fails later, at :126 where dead==3 && c.calls==1 after the resurrected object is collected, or at :164 where c.calls==16 for sixteen finalizable objects). The learner predicts, then records, the OR_CHECK line in object_runtime.ephemeron_graph or object_runtime.finalizers that rejects each. No flawed implementation is supplied in the learner tree; the assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once the learner builds one of the variants above (no supplied artifact demonstrates it): a closure that loses a value breaks the liveness invariant, visible as a live mask short of 15 on the reverse-ordered chain, and a driver that can finalize twice breaks the at-most-once invariant, visible as a callback count or finalized mask other than one. It is not proved-impact because the model has no real resource, secret or authority, and it is not a crash or sanitizer finding because the failure is a wrong answer from well-defined C.
security_lab.remediation: Run strong and ephemeron closure to a joint fixed point, clear weak references before retaining finalizable objects, set the finalized bit before calling the callback, and keep cleanup budgeted. The regression that rejects the original input is the existing object_runtime.ephemeron_graph (value-to-key cycle must give dead==15) together with object_runtime.finalizers (calls==1, finalized==1); the learner must also retain the reverse-ordered chain and resurrection-then-reclamation cases as additional CHECKs.
security_lab.limitations: The demonstration shows wrong reachability and callback accounting on at most 16 identities, not exploitability against a real runtime, arbitrary code execution, or the finalization policy of Lua or CPython. A crash or sanitizer report during the work would be a separate, lower impact class. Bounded enumeration does not prove every graph, and the 25,600-row comparison exists only if the learner writes the model, and no concurrency, hostile allocator or corrupted-state case is covered.
