security_lab.adversary: The attacker chooses the synthetic reference graph (16 identities, two strong edge fields each), the external-root counts (up to 255), which identities are submitted as trial candidates, the queued decrements (up to 8) and, in the concurrent variant, the interleaving of retain, release and collection calls through the adapter. The attacker does not write the stored counts directly, forge trial tokens or generations, or alias outputs with the owner.
security_lab.violated_property: Safety against premature reclamation and leaks in reference counting: an object with an external reference from outside the candidate set (counts 2,1 on a two-object cycle) must survive, a true cycle with counts 1,1 and no external root must be reclaimed, and the invariant that each live count equals roots plus incoming edges plus queued decrements must hold at every operation boundary.
security_lab.boundary: Single process on the synthetic 16-slot owner with at most 255 roots per identity and 8 queued decrements, built under Debug, Release and ASan/UBSan. Only object_runtime.rc_concurrent starts threads: it creates and joins POSIX worker threads (tests/rc_ext.c:200, 214 and 242; the last worker runs 1000 retain/release pairs while the owner thread runs 1000 prepare/commit rounds) that reach the owner only through the mutex adapter the learner implements. No test forks a child or opens a file or socket. Success is a wrong live set or count on synthetic objects.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) CTest object_runtime.trial (tests/tests.c, trial): a candidate cycle with refs 1,1,1 gives dead==3 and live==4 while refs[2]==1, and refs 2,1 gives dead==0, live==3 with refs[0]==2 and refs[1]==1; a zero residual count returns OR_INVALID. (a) object_runtime.rc_zero (tests/rc_ext.c, zero): two edges a->b release to dead==3 with orr_invariant(&h) true, release without a root returns OR_STATE with the heap bytes unchanged, the 255-root limit returns OR_FULL unchanged, and the 48-identity limit returns OR_FULL. (a) object_runtime.rc_deferred (deferred): eight queued decrements then a ninth returns OR_FULL unchanged, orr_flush budgets 0 and 1, and a two-object cycle yields candidates==3 and orr_prepare gives t.dead==3. (a) object_runtime.rc_concurrent (concurrent): orrc_call serializes a retain/release worker thread against the owner thread, then r.trial.dead==3 and r.dead==3. The oracle mode (`object-runtime-rc oracle`, tests/rc_ext.c:261-308) is not a registered CTest and compares nothing: it prints one row 'R graph mask mode live refs0 refs1 refs2' for each of 4096 graphs x 8 root masks x 2 release modes = 65,536 cases, which the learner compares with an independent model of their own. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own trial deletion, each stated as a property to break: one that reclaims an object still referenced from outside the candidate set (the refs 2,1 case at tests/tests.c:234 requires dead==0 and unchanged counts), and one that reclaims an object reachable only from a candidate whose residual count is positive. The learner predicts, then records, which OR_CHECK line in object_runtime.trial (tests/tests.c:226 or :234) rejects each. No flawed implementation is supplied in the learner tree; the assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once the learner builds one of the variants above (no supplied artifact demonstrates it): the variant reclaims an object that the tests keep alive (a nonzero dead mask where the refs 2,1 case requires dead==0), breaking the count invariant checked by orr_invariant. It is not proved-impact because no freed memory is reused by an attacker, and a stale access caught only by ASan would be a sanitizer-finding.
security_lab.remediation: Subtract only candidate-internal edges from copied counts, rescue everything reachable from positive residuals, and apply decrements to surviving targets. The regression that rejects the original input is object_runtime.trial (refs 2,1 must give dead==0) plus object_runtime.rc_deferred and rc_concurrent; the learner adds a CHECK for the outside-candidate reference case.
security_lab.limitations: This shows a count or reclamation error on a finite synthetic heap, not use-after-free exploitation, arbitrary code execution, or correctness of a production reference counter. The mutex adapter provides exclusion only for the documented calls; atomic counts, memory-order claims and unbounded schedules are not demonstrated.

security_lab.target: labs/object_runtime/src/object_runtime_vm.c (root-map and derived-reference relocation adapter) declared in labs/object_runtime/include/object_runtime_vm.h, and the or_safepoint kernel in labs/object_runtime/src/object_runtime.c; the original runtime.vm collector is consumed unchanged and is not the attacked component.
security_lab.adversary: The attacker supplies the synthetic root map for a frame (slot offsets, lengths, tagged versus scalar slots), derived-reference offsets including the one-past offset, the registration order and the relocation target base. The attacker does not supply raw heap addresses, forge registration tickets, or execute during a pause beyond the documented calls.
security_lab.violated_property: Modelled heap/lifetime integrity of moving collection (CVM references are index-and-generation pairs into a fixed heap, not machine addresses): every root copy and derived reference must relocate together with its base, scalar slots must not change, an offset beyond one-past (offset 9 against length 8) must reject the whole frame unchanged, and no stale copy may remain usable after relocation.
security_lab.boundary: Hosted, serialized, allocation-free calls on a synthetic CVM heap and a 16-cell registration pool, built under Debug, Release and ASan/UBSan and driven by object_runtime.safepoint, vm_roots and vm_foreign only. These cases are single-threaded and start no child process or file or socket (tests/vm_ext.c; the pthread backend in tests/foreign_backend.c is linked only into the extensions executable, CMakeLists.txt:112-117, not the object-runtime-vm target at :79-85). The LLVM statepoint artifact is a separate compiler-dependent deliverable and no security demonstration is claimed for it. Success is a stale or partially relocated synthetic value.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) CTest object_runtime.safepoint (tests/tests.c, safepoint): with forward[1]=5 a map missing a tagged slot returns OR_INVALID, the full map gives slot[0].base==5, slot[1].base==5, offset==8 and scalar slot[2].scalar==2, and offset 9 returns OR_INVALID with memcmp(&f,&before,sizeof f)==0. (a) object_runtime.vm_roots (tests/vm_ext.c, roots): an unregistered old copy yields cvm_field(&v,old,0,&field)==CVM_STALE while the registered copy reads 77, a duplicate register returns OR_STATE, a failing collect leaves the Cvm bytes unchanged, a 216-slot map relocates every copy (stats.slots==216), unregistering a stale ticket returns OR_MISS. (a) object_runtime.vm_foreign (foreign): a callback during orv_call leaves registered(&o)==0 and o.foreign==0, a failed callback keeps its completed allocation but not output or roots, and pool exhaustion rolls back with OR_FULL. The oracle mode (`object-runtime-vm oracle`, tests/vm_ext.c:283-381) is not a registered CTest: it prints rows of relocation results and compares nothing, so the learner compares them with an independent model of their own. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own adapter, each stated as a property to break: a relocation after which some root copy still holds the old base (a tagged slot absent from the map is accepted, or a registered copy is not updated), and a relocation that changes part of a frame before it rejects an invalid map or offset (tests/tests.c:263 requires memcmp(&f,&before,sizeof f)==0 after offset 9). The learner predicts, then records, which OR_CHECK line in object_runtime.safepoint (tests/tests.c:255-263) or object_runtime.vm_roots rejects each. No flawed implementation is supplied in the learner tree; the assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once the learner builds one of the variants above (no supplied artifact demonstrates it): a non-transactional or incomplete relocation leaves a stale base or a partially updated frame that the tests detect (memcmp change, CVM_STALE read). It is not proved-impact because the stale value never reaches attacker-controlled memory, and an out-of-bounds access seen only under ASan would be a sanitizer-finding.
security_lab.remediation: Validate the entire map and every registration before mutating, relocate all copies including derived and one-past offsets, preserve scalars, and leave the frame byte-identical on rejection. The regression that rejects the original input is object_runtime.safepoint (omitted root and offset 9 must be OR_INVALID with unchanged bytes) plus object_runtime.vm_roots.
security_lab.limitations: The demonstration covers adapter logic on a small synthetic frame and the supplied CVM, not an LLVM statepoint pipeline, concurrent or interrupt-time collection, or exploitation of a real moving collector. Unregistered copies and forged tickets are outside the contract.

security_lab.target: labs/object_runtime/src/object_runtime_ext.c (ORXIntern weak binary-symbol table) declared in labs/object_runtime/include/object_runtime_ext.h; the attacked component is the learner implementation.
security_lab.adversary: The attacker controls counted binary keys of length 0..15 (for example {0,97} and {97,0}: folding hash=(hash*33+byte) mod 256 from 0 gives 97 and 129, which differ by 32 and so are congruent modulo 4, 8 and 16 and share a probe start under the assumption, not stated by the contract, that the probe start is hash mod capacity, equivalently hash & (capacity-1); EXTENSIONS.md:101-102 says only linear probing), the order of intern, retain, release, collect, pack and sweep calls, and the laboratory allocation-failure schedule. The attacker cannot corrupt controls, manufacture allocator pointers, alias inputs with outputs or reenter allocator callbacks.
security_lab.violated_property: Identity integrity: distinct byte keys must receive distinct handles even when their hashes collide, a dead generation must never be revived or reused after sweep, and a failed growth must leave the old table, heap and handle unchanged.
security_lab.boundary: Single-threaded runs on the synthetic heap with a counting test allocator (ow_allocator with fail_at), buckets growing only 4 to 8 to 16, built under Debug, Release and ASan/UBSan and driven by object_runtime.ext_intern. The ext_intern case starts no thread or child process and opens no file or socket; its only host interaction is allocation through the counting ow_allocator of the ownership component. (The ext_foreign case in the same executable joins a pthread backend, tests/extensions.c:235-293, and is not evidence for this exercise.) Harmless success is one key's handle returned for another key or a dead handle accepted.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) CTest object_runtime.ext_intern (tests/extensions.c, intern): keys x={0,97} and y={97,0} receive handles with !eq(first,second); an injected allocation failure on a third key returns OR_FULL with the heap bytes, bucket pointer and a.live unchanged and the first key still hits with eq(out,first); after release, collect (dead==1) a lookup of x returns OR_INVALID until orx_intern_sweep removes one entry; orx_pack moves cells without changing the foreign-pinned bytes {0,97}; a failed orx_intern_reserve(16) leaves capacity 8; reinterning y gives the same slot but a different generation (out.generation != second.generation); and a full pool unwinds the private bucket allocation (a.live==0). The oracle mode of the same executable (tests/extensions.c:296-363) is not a registered CTest: it prints allocation-failure (I) rows plus pack (P) and binary32 (V) rows (tests/extensions.c:296-363) and compares nothing, so the learner compares the rows with a model of their own. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own table, each stated as a property to break: one that returns the same handle for two different keys that share a probe start (tests/extensions.c:167 requires !eq(first,second)), and one that hands back the old generation after a sweep (:207-208 requires out.generation != second.generation, and :183 requires OR_INVALID for the collected but unswept x). The learner predicts, then records, which OR_CHECK line in object_runtime.ext_intern rejects each. No flawed implementation is supplied in the learner tree; the assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once the learner builds one of the variants above (no supplied artifact demonstrates it): a table that compares too little returns equal handles for unequal keys, and one that reuses a generation accepts a dead handle; both are visible in the !eq and generation checks. It is not proved-impact because the confusion grants no authority beyond a synthetic table, and it is not a crash or sanitizer finding because it occurs through well-defined C.
security_lab.remediation: Compare full length and bytes after probing, reject get and reserve while the table is collected but unswept, retire generations at sweep, and stage replacement buckets before allocating the symbol. The regression that rejects the original input is object_runtime.ext_intern (colliding pair distinct, stale x rejected with OR_INVALID, reintern of y gets a new generation, injected growth failure unchanged).
security_lab.limitations: This shows identity conflation in a 16-bucket synthetic table, not hash-flooding denial of service against a real intern table, a timing side channel, or memory corruption. Cooperative in-process handles do not resist arbitrary memory writes, and allocator behavior beyond the injected failures is not modeled.

The attacker does not supply host addresses, corrupt descriptors, forge generations or run arbitrary machine code.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of property lookup: a cache hit must return the current value from the currently resolved holder (a prototype change from A to B must yield 20, not the stale 10), and a getter that defines receiver.key1=99 yet returns 42 must leave 99 visible on the next lookup. The direct rz_forward (src/resilience.c:56) is not called by resilience.pressure (tests/tests.c:29-62), and no test calls it directly; registered tests reach it only indirectly, through the learner's pump and adapter code that PRESSURE.md:25 and OUTBOX.md:65 require to call it. The `resilience-pressure policy` and `pump` modes (pressure_test.c:366 and :429, selected at :556-562) are unregistered instruments that print one row per case and compare nothing; the learner runs them and compares the rows with their own model of the five policies and of pump progress. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own implementation, each stated as a property to break: an owned-value pump whose forward step removes the queue head even when the channel refuses it (resilience.pressure_owned, through the RZ_FULL step at pressure_test.c:274, check_balance and c.made==c.dropped), and an offer path that enqueues after the scope deadline has passed (resilience.pressure rejects an expired BLOCK offer at tests/tests.c:55-61 with the queue unchanged, and the pump's expiry result is checked at pressure_test.c:329). security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation, reached only once the learner builds one of the variants above (no supplied artifact demonstrates it): the variant loses, duplicates or reorders synthetic messages or admits after expiry, observable in the queue snapshot or the made/dropped counters. It is not proved-impact because no real service is starved, and a crash or sanitizer finding in the same code would be a lower class.

Raw aliases, malicious allocator callbacks and concurrent mutation are outside the bounded contract, and the blocked offer is a retained operation, not a thread.

security_lab.target: labs/resilience/src/resilience.c (RZReceiver), labs/resilience/src/journal_follow.c (append-only journal and recovery, RzjJournal) and labs/resilience/followthrough/journal_posix.c (file adapter); the attacked component is the learner implementation.
security_lab.adversary: The attacker is an authenticated-model client (IDs 0 and 1) that replays or reorders requests with chosen client, id, fence and delta values, changes parameters under a reused id, presents stale fencing tokens, and waits past the retention window; in the journal variant the schedule chooses the crash point around record and effect publication. The attacker does not forge client identity, write the receiver state or choose the fence issuer.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of a synthetic total: an effect must apply at most once within retention (client 0, id 1, fence 2, delta 3 gives total 3 once, replay returns 3), a changed delta under the same id must CONFLICT, a lower fence must be rejected at the protected receiver, and a crash must not leave an effect without its record or the reverse after replay recovery.
security_lab.boundary: Local runs built under Debug, Release and ASan/UBSan and driven by resilience.receiver and resilience.receiver_journal. resilience.receiver is a single-threaded in-memory model with a 4-record table. resilience.receiver_journal runs the journal over an in-memory test device with injected cut points and, in native_file (followthrough/journal_test.c:384-429), over a file made with mkstemp under /tmp and unlinked at once (:386-388), written and fdatasync'd through journal_posix.c, plus a forked child that applies one effect and calls _exit without delivering the reply (:400-410), which the parent reaps with waitpid (:413). No socket or thread is used and no host storage setting is changed. Harmless success is a doubled or lost synthetic total.
security_lab.expected_evidence: (a) CTest resilience.receiver (tests/tests.c, receiver): client 0 id 1 fence 2 delta 3 at tick 0 gives out==3; its replay at tick 1 returns 3 with duplicate==true and r.total==3; delta 4 under the same id returns RZ_CONFLICT with r.total==3; client 1 fence 1 returns RZ_STALE; retention 4 lets the same id apply again at tick 4 with out==6. (a) resilience.receiver_journal (followthrough/journal_test.c, the registered `test` mode): main (:558-577) runs nominal, failure_cuts, replica, recovery_cuts, native_file and invalid_progress in order and prints 'journal tests passed' once, after all six return (:576). failure_cuts (:240-306) injects a cut at each of 68 write positions in 3 modes for both apply and issue, and requires that a write reported RZJ_UNCERTAIN leaves the poisoned journal with receiver.total==0 (:266-267), that recovery then shows total 0 or 3, and that a replay returns 3 with duplicate matching whether the effect committed. nominal (:173-238) rejects a stale fence in the journal (:197-199). replica (:308-358) is a supplied demonstration of the stale-fence hazard: writer a issues fence 5 and applies delta 3; writer b, opened from a copy taken when only fence 4 had been issued, still accepts fence 4 with delta 7, so the totals are 3 and 7, and rzj_mirror must return RZJ_CORRUPT instead of silently merging the divergent effect (:326-332); a then rejects fence 4 with RZ_STALE (:339-341). The journal's `oracle` and `cuts` modes (:495-556, selected at :560-568) read cases on stdin and print the durable image in hex; they are not registered CTests and compare nothing, so the learner compares their bytes with their own byte-level model. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own implementation, each stated as a property to break. First, an effect becomes visible in receiver.total before its record is durable: the in-memory rz_receive (tests/tests.c:195-210) has no durability boundary and cannot show this, so it is observable only through the journal's injected cuts (failure_cuts, :266-267) and the recovery checks that follow. Second, a receiver that accepts a fence lower than one already issued (resilience.receiver rejects client 1 with fence 1 at tests/tests.c:207, and nominal rejects it in the journal at journal_test.c:197-199). The learner predicts, then records, which RZ_CHECK line rejects each. Apart from the replica demonstration above, no flawed implementation is supplied in the learner tree; the assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation. A supplied artifact demonstrates the stale-fence form: replica() (journal_test.c:308-341) produces two writers with totals 3 and 7 and requires rzj_mirror to return RZJ_CORRUPT. The double-apply, lost-effect and accepted-stale-fence forms in the receiver itself are reached only once the learner builds the variants above. It is not proved-impact because no real balance or durable store is affected.
security_lab.remediation: Publish effect, record, fence and reply as one transition, return the original reply on identical replay, report CONFLICT on changed parameters, check the fence at the receiver, never evict a live record, and make journal recovery idempotent at every cut. The regression that rejects the original input is resilience.receiver (replay total stays 3, CONFLICT, STALE, expiry gives 6) plus resilience.receiver_journal (cuts and recovery).
security_lab.limitations: This shows duplicate-effect and stale-token errors in a bounded model, not indefinite exactly-once execution, durability across real power loss, authentication, or globally monotonic fence issuance. The in-memory anchor does not survive a crash and the journal is a teaching device.

(a) resilience.service_outbox (followthrough/outbox_test.c, the registered `test` mode): nominal, extended_identity, cuts, invalid_recovery and native in order, then 'RZ outbox passed' once (:508-522). Its `oracle` mode (:443-506, selected at :524) is not registered, reads cases on stdin, prints one row per case and compares nothing, so the learner compares it with their own model. (a) resilience.service_io (service_io_test.c, `test`: parser, native_partial_and_duplicate, failures, blocked_reply and queued_burst, :514-522), where six queued frames yield four effects and two RZ_FULL replies before effect (:430). (a) resilience.service_transport (composition_test.c, `test`, tests() at :168-252): it sweeps 4096 mask, second-mask and deadline histories and requires applied<=1, total==(applied?3:0), dispatched<=capacity, tokens+dispatched==capacity, balanced response allocation, deliveries==applied*(1+reset_before_ack) and acknowledged==applied; it also injects each of 4 allocation-failure positions and 45 journal write refusals. The `oracle` and `layout` modes (composition_test.c:254 and :366, selected at :397-405) are not registered: oracle reads 11-field cases on stdin and prints one row each, layout prints structure sizes, and neither compares anything. COMPOSITION.md:116-117 asks the learner to compare all 19 exported oracle fields against an independent model of their own. (c) The learner builds two variants of their own implementation, each stated as a property to break, both named by COMPOSITION.md:122: a due time or deadline converted to wheel ticks by rounding down, so that a retry can dispatch before it is due (COMPOSITION.md:65-66 requires rounding up), and a restart that loses a notification recovered from the journal (deliveries must equal applied*(1+reset_before_ack) and acknowledged must equal applied, composition_test.c:212-214). No flawed implementation is supplied in the learner tree; the assessor's mutation set also checks this invariant.

Token spending is not rolled back on later failure by design, and the small finite permit identities bound the anchor's lifetime.

security_lab.adversary: Controls the movement input history (-1, 0 or 1, length 0..8), a changed input to replay, the allocation-failure ordinal 1..6 during rp_checkpoint, and may cause the replay to be invoked again; does not control the random seed constant, code, native pointers or any real effect target.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of deterministic replay and atomic checkpoint: replaying from a snapshot equals a fresh fold of the corrected inputs, effects are returned as data and applied at most once per (timeline,tick), and a failed checkpoint leaves the published root and used count unchanged.
security_lab.boundary: Hosted Linux x86-64 teaching build in a disposable build directory. replicated.replay (replay_test, tests/tests.c:233-270) runs in one process: at most 8 steps, 6 checkpoint cut ordinals, histories checked against a Python integer model that you write. replicated.replay_native (replay_depth/native.c:142-230, CTest timeout 60 s) does not: it creates an AF_UNIX socketpair and forks a sender child, forks a second child that applies one effect to a durable inbox and exits with status 42, reaps both with waitpid, and creates two log files with mkstemp under /tmp (cmastery-replay-XXXXXX) that it unlinks at once. replicated.replay_counterexamples and tests/effect_adapter.c keep their synthetic effect counters in process memory and write only to stdout. No network is used and no real effect target exists.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Backed by CTest replicated.replay (replay_test in labs/replicated/tests/tests.c): rp_step from (0,0,0,1) with movement -1 gives position 15, score 0 and random 1015568748, then movement 1 gives position 0, score 3 and effect tick 2; rp_replay of the eight inputs gives tick 8 and score 12; replaying the first three inputs and then the corrected suffix equals a fresh fold of the corrected inputs (position, score, random); rp_checkpoint with failure ordinals 1..6 returns RP_FAILED, leaves the candidate root at 99 and arena.used unchanged, and the old root still reads value 0, while ordinal 0 succeeds. Supplied evidence for the replay and effect hazards: the registered replicated.replay_counterexamples (replay_depth/oracle_driver.c:118-160) runs a deliberately flawed reducer whose hidden random state is omitted from the replay snapshot, so the first fold and the replay differ (CHECK first != replay), and its external-effect half is a scripted illustration, not a computed delivery: it increments a synthetic counter once for an effect struct (timeline 9, tick 1) and once for a copy of it, two inline increments with no callback or adapter involved (oracle_driver.c:141-153), so the count of 2 holds by construction (it prints REPLAY_COUNTEREXAMPLES ... external-effect-count2), whereas the hidden-random divergence is genuinely computed (:118-140). The learner-compilable labs/replicated/tests/effect_adapter.c is not a CTest target (only tools/run_replicated_experiments.py builds it): its receiver, keyed by tick, yields deduplicated_effects=8, failure_prefix=3 and conflicting_reuse=rejected, but its unsafe_replay_effects=16 is a counting loop that never calls an adapter (effect_adapter.c:45-49), so that counter is not evidence of a duplicated effect. Variants to build yourself, stated as the properties to break: a step whose replayed score depends on state the snapshot does not carry, and a checkpoint that changes the arena or the published root when it fails. Predict the first failing CHECK (tests.c:244-247 for the score, tests.c:253-255 for the suffix replay, tests.c:261-263 for the checkpoint) and record the line replicated.replay prints. The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation: the divergent hidden-random replay is shown by the supplied replicated.replay_counterexamples, where both folds are computed (oracle_driver.c:118-140), whereas its external-effect-count2 is only a scripted illustration of the duplicate-effect hazard (two inline increments on a struct and its copy, :141-153) and not a demonstrated duplicate delivery; a leaked allocation or a score that disagrees with a fresh fold is shown only once the learner builds and runs a variant. All of it is a visible broken invariant in the teaching reducer; it is not undefined behaviour and the effect target is a synthetic in-process counter, so no real impact is proved.
security_lab.remediation: Keep rp_step pure, return effects as data, publish both HAMT updates under one root and roll back on failure, and deduplicate effects by an idempotency key in the adapter. The regression that rejects the original defective input is CTest replicated.replay (the score 3, score 12, suffix-equals-fresh and arena.used==old CHECKs); extend the effect adapter test with a (timeline,tick) key as the brief asks.
security_lab.limitations: The synthetic adapter shows the duplicate-effect hazard only; it does not show real external side effects, durable snapshot recovery, a concurrent adapter, or the full replay snapshot (tick and random remain in RPState).

security_lab.target: labs/corpus_ring (cr_build, cr_owner, cr_change, replica selection and migration plan, src/ and ring.h)
security_lab.adversary: Chooses token positions, owner labels, ordinals, availability masks, byte keys and the order of membership changes (including equal positions and capacity-filling lists); does not control the hash component, the code, native pointers, or forge a ring value after cr_build admitted it.
security_lab.violated_property: Integrity of placement: lookup is the clockwise successor under the exact tie order, replicas are distinct available physical owners, a change moves only the keys of the one owner, and a failed build, change or plan publishes nothing (epoch and output unchanged).
security_lab.boundary: Hosted Linux x86-64 teaching build in a disposable build directory. The four registered anchors run as ring_tests (tests.c:140-153) in one process on in-memory structs: at most 32 tokens, owners 1..16, uint16 positions, a nonzero uint32 epoch; the membership anchor loops over all 65,536 keys twice (tests.c:52-58, 73-78); the routing anchor uses an in-process hash callback (tests.c:109-121). No test forks, opens a socket or file, creates a thread or uses the network, and no data is moved, authenticated or transported. The corpus_ring.oracle test and the mutation tests are built only when an assessor root is supplied and are not part of the supplied suite.
security_lab.expected_evidence: Backed by the four anchors in labs/corpus_ring/tests.c (CTest corpus_ring.lookup, .membership, .replicas, .routing). lookup: with tokens {100,3,0},{100,2,0},{20,1,0},{100,2,1}, cr_owner returns owner 2 for key 100 (tie order by owner then ordinal), owner 1 for keys 101, 65535 and 20, a duplicate token identity makes cr_build return CR_INVALID with the ring unchanged, and an empty ring returns CR_EMPTY with the output unchanged. membership: for tokens {10,1,0},{30,2,0} adding owner 3 at {20,3,0},{40,3,1}, cr_change with abort cut 0..4 returns CR_ABORTED leaving the ring byte-identical, the full change gives epoch 8, a lookup with the old epoch returns CR_STALE, every one of 65536 keys has the same owner or owner 3, cr_plan returns CR_FULL with n unchanged for capacity 0 and for capacity 1 (where the moves array is also compared unchanged, tests.c:64-66) and CR_OK with 4 moves, all to owner 3, for capacity 9, and an epoch of UINT32_MAX returns CR_FULL unchanged. replicas: with tokens {10,1,0},{20,1,1},{30,2,0},{40,3,0}, three replicas are owners 1,2,3, a down mask of 1 gives 2,3, and mask 1 with three replicas returns CR_UNAVAILABLE with the output unchanged. routing: a hash callback failing through its context returns CR_HASH_FAILED with the output unchanged. Variants to build yourself, stated as the properties to break: for each anchor, design your own defect that falsifies one property it guards (tie order and duplicate identity for lookup; abort atomicity, stale-epoch rejection and minimal movement for membership; distinct available physical owners for replicas; hash failure for routing). Predict the CR_CHECK line that should fail (lookup 21 or 27, membership 47-48, 51 or 57, replicas 96-99 or 102-103, routing 133-134), run the matching anchor and record the line printed. The assessor's mutation set also checks these invariants.
security_lab.impact_class: demonstrated-invariant-violation (only once the learner builds and runs a variant; no supplied artifact demonstrates it): duplicate physical replicas, stale routing or load captured by chosen tokens is an observable broken placement property on synthetic membership; it is not a crash or undefined behaviour and does not prove Sybil resistance or any deployed impact.
security_lab.remediation: Validate identities and counts in cr_build, apply the exact (position,owner,ordinal) tie order, skip repeated physical owners and unavailable owners, publish epoch and migration rows only after all checks pass, and surface hash failure. The regressions that reject the original defective inputs are CTest corpus_ring.lookup, corpus_ring.membership, corpus_ring.replicas and corpus_ring.routing; run each against the matching learner-built variant.
security_lab.limitations: Does not show Sybil resistance, Byzantine tolerance, authenticated membership, safe data movement, load balance for adversarial hashes or arbitrary code execution; reads trust an admitted ring and do not revalidate forged public fields.
